content: Visitors to healthcare facilities are currently limited due to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic to ensure public safety. The number of visitors allowed may vary depending on specific circumstances, and certain precautions are recommended by the CDC to minimize risks. 1. A designated entrance should be established specifically for visitors to control access effectively. 2. Visitors displaying symptoms of acute respiratory illness, such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath, should leave the facility immediately and seek medical care if necessary. 3. All visitors should be vigilant about recognizing signs and symptoms of respiratory illness and refrain from entering healthcare facilities if they exhibit such symptoms. 4. Visual alerts, such as signs and posters, should be placed at facility entrances and other strategic locations to instruct visitors not to enter if they have a fever or respiratory symptoms. These alerts should also include information about COVID-19 symptoms and whom to notify if symptoms develop. 5. Visitors are strongly discouraged from visiting patients who are at high risk for severe illness from COVID-19, including older adults and individuals with underlying medical conditions. 6. Healthy visitors should wear appropriate face coverings, such as surgical masks, rather than homemade masks, to reduce the risk of transmission. 7. Facilities should provide alternative communication options, such as video or audio calls, for patients in isolation to connect with their loved ones. 8. Staff members should be available to provide training and education to visitors on infection prevention measures. Visitors permitted to enter healthcare facilities should be educated on the following: Recognizing signs and symptoms of COVID-19 and understanding whom to notify if symptoms develop. Proper hand hygiene techniques, including washing hands with soap and water for at least 40 seconds or using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer containing at least 60% ethanol or 70% isopropanol for at least 20 seconds. Respiratory hygiene practices, such as covering the mouth and nose with a disposable tissue when coughing or sneezing, and disposing of the tissue properly. Healthcare facilities should ensure adequate supplies are available for visitors to perform hand hygiene and respiratory hygiene. Visitors with respiratory symptoms should be instructed to leave the facility immediately and seek medical care if needed. If you wish to help others during the COVID-19 pandemic, there are several ways to contribute while maintaining safety precautions. Volunteering and helping others can improve your own mental and physical well-being, reduce stress, and even boost immunity. Here are some ways to assist: 1. Prioritize your own physical and mental health to ensure you can effectively help others. 2. Follow social distancing and sanitation guidelines to prevent the spread of the virus. 3. Check on your neighbors, especially those who may be vulnerable or isolated. 4. Make donations to support those in need. 5. Volunteer at facilities where your expertise is required, ensuring you adhere to safety protocols. 6. Donate essential items such as blood, food, and other necessities. 7. Combat misinformation by sharing accurate information online. 8. Share positive news and updates with your family and community to foster hope and resilience. If you wish to accompany a family member or friend to their medical appointments or procedures because you are concerned they may need your support, it is important to note that hospitals are currently restricting visitors. You should check with your local healthcare facility for specific guidelines and recommendations regarding hospital visits in your situation.
